issues.failure_explanation: The theorem defines W_[k](t) = W_[k-1](a_k t) W_[k-1]((1-2a_k)t) W_[k-1](a_k t) (a Suzuki triple jump of a symmetric order-2k scheme) and asserts order 2k+2. The triple jump has order 2k+2 only if the first failed order condition 2a_k^{2k+1} + (1-2a_k)^{2k+1} = 0 holds, i.e. a_k = 1/(2+c_k) with c_k^{2k+1} = -2, so a_k = 1/(2 + 2^{1/(2k+1)} e^{±πi/(2k+1)}). The printed formula equals 1/(1 + 2^{1/(2k+1)} e^{∓πi/(2k+1)}), a different number: for k=1 it evaluates to a_1 ≈ 0.4236 + 0.2836i, whereas the correct coefficient is 1/(2+2^{1/3}e^{±iπ/3}) ≈ 0.3244 ± 0.1346i — exactly the value the theorem itself prints ('where a = 0.324396 + 0.134586i'). With the coefficients as printed, the order conditions fail (for k=1, 2a^3 + (1-2a)^3 ≈ -0.196 - 0.314i ≠ 0), so the schemes defined by the printed formula do not have the claimed orders.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coefficient definition in (\ref{HO53}) by the correct Suzuki value a_k = 1/(2 + 2^{1/(2k+1)} e^{±πi/(2k+1)}), which reproduces the theorem's own decimal values; with that single correction every statement of the theorem (orders, term counts, displayed expansions) holds as written.
issues.overall_effect: The order claims of Theorem thm:added-1 (order 4, 6, 8 for W_[1], W_[2], W_[3]) are false for the schemes as defined by the printed formula, and the theorem is internally inconsistent (the closed form contradicts its own decimal coefficients and the displayed expansions, which match the correct coefficients). The companion theorems splitU and thm:added-2 contain the analogous correct formulas and are unaffected.
issues.title: Triple-jump coefficient formula in Theorem thm:added-1 is mathematically wrong
issues.why_classification: A one-line replacement of the closed form, forced by the theorem's own numerical values and the cited source [JD6, Thm 2.3], restores every stated order and all displayed expansions; no substantive claim or rate is lost, so the repair is short, local, and routine.

issues.failure_explanation: The display asserts that W_[2](t), the 19-term expansion shown, is the scheme of order 6 generated by the recursion W_[2](t) = W_[1](a_2 t)W_[1]((1-2a_2)t)W_[1](a_2 t). Expanding this composition (with a_1 = 0.3244+0.1346i, a_2 = 1/(2+2^{1/5}e^{iπ/5}) ≈ 0.3241+0.0747i) and merging adjacent e^{tK_2}-factors, the e^{tK_1}-coefficients are a_2[a_1, 1-2a_1, a_1], (1-2a_2)[a_1, 1-2a_1, a_1], a_2[a_1, 1-2a_1, a_1]; hence the central coefficient is d = (1-2a_2)(1-2a_1) ≈ 0.0830 - 0.1471i, not 1-2a = 0.8098 - 0.1357i. With the printed d, the sum of the K_1-coefficients is 4a+2b+2c+d ≈ 1.7265 - 0.1339i ≠ 1, so the displayed product is not even consistent (V'(0) ≠ K_1+K_2), let alone of order 6. The theorem's later 55-term display is consistent only with the correct d (its printed d ≈ 0.0348 - 0.0436i equals a_3·(1-2a_2)(1-2a_1)), confirming the printed value is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the printed value to d = (1-2a_2)(1-2a_1) ≈ 0.0830 - 0.1471i (equivalently, recompute the display from the recursion already stated in the theorem); the 19-term display then satisfies all stated claims.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed 19-term formula for W_[2] in Theorem thm:added-1, taken literally, is not the claimed order-6 splitting (it is not even first-order accurate); the order-6 guarantee for that displayed scheme fails. The recursion, the remaining coefficients, and the other schemes are unaffected once d is corrected.
issues.title: Central coefficient of the displayed 19-term scheme W_[2] is wrong (d = 1-2a)
issues.why_classification: A single coefficient must be recomputed from the recursion already stated in the same theorem; the corrected display satisfies the order and count claims, so the repair is local, requires only a contained computation, and preserves all substantive guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: Part (c) of Remark remApp claims to realize one step of the order-3 splitting V_3(t/n) = e^{α(t/2n)K_2} e^{α(t/n)K_1} e^{(t/2n)K_2} e^{ᾱ(t/n)K_1} e^{ᾱ(t/2n)K_2} of Proposition prop333. Steps (1), (2), (3) and (5) chain the outputs correctly, but step (4) applies the fourth exponential e^{α(t/n)K_1} to x_k instead of to x_{k+ᾱ}, the output of step (2). The composed map of the printed iteration is therefore not the product of the five exponentials (the intermediate x_{k+ᾱ} produced by step (2) is discarded by the x-flow), so the iteration does not approximate the flow of K_1+K_2 with the advertised order Ct^4/n^3; the printed construction fails its stated guarantee.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In step (4), use the output of step (2) as input, i.e. x_{k+1} = σ_{y_{k+1/2}}(ta/n, x_{k+ā}); the printed iteration is then exactly the composition of the five exponentials of Proposition prop333 and the order Ct^4/n^3 guarantee holds.
issues.overall_effect: The third-order algorithm of Remark remApp(c) is invalid as written; the advertised order Ct^4/n^3 does not hold for the printed iteration, and any 2-D third-order computations performed with it do not have the claimed accuracy. The remaining algorithms in the remark are unaffected.
issues.title: Third-order coordinate algorithm restarts from x_k in step (4), so it does not implement V_3
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol repair (feeding x_{k+ᾱ} into step (4)) makes the printed iteration exactly the composition of Proposition prop333's five exponentials, after which the stated order and all uses of the algorithm survive; no new argument or construction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The numerical results in Tables~\ref{lokRmse}, \ref{van}, and \ref{lor} demonstrate that approximation accuracy, measured by RMSE, depends on both the number of iterations \( n \) and the order of the splitting method.
we observe that the number of terms grows rapidly with both the dimension and the order of the method. This substantial increase leads to greater complexity in the approximation.
Number of exponential terms involved in N-dimensional splittings of order $p$

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion asserts the splitting method is 'more computationally efficient' than RK45 and that this efficiency 'arise[s] from decomposing the original problem into smaller sub-problems... significantly reducing the computational cost, especially for high-dimensional systems.' The paper contains no runtime, operation-count, or cost measurement of any kind: the only quantitative comparisons offered are RMSE accuracy tables (Tables lokRmse, van, lor). Furthermore, the paper's own exponential-term analysis (Section expHI, Table tabNterms) shows the per-step cost of its higher-order schemes explodes with order and dimension (e.g. 8193 exponentials per step for the 14th-order 2-D scheme, 145 for the 6th-order 3-D scheme), which is in tension with the advertised efficiency 'especially for high-dimensional systems'. Thus the prose claims a cost advantage the paper never establishes.

failure_location.quote: Compared to classical schemes such as the Runge--Kutta method (e.g., RK45 with the absolute and relative tolerances of $10^{-16}$), the splitting method is not only competitive in accuracy but also more computationally efficient.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Hedge or remove the efficiency claim (e.g. state only that the method is competitive in accuracy and that its cost structure per sub-problem is simple), or support it with an actual cost/runtime comparison; no formal result depends on the claim.
issues.overall_effect: The efficiency claim of Section sec:conclusions is unsupported; only accuracy competitiveness is demonstrated. Readers relying on the stated efficiency guarantee for high-dimensional or high-order settings are misled; all formal results are unaffected.
issues.title: Conclusion claims computational efficiency over RK45 without any supporting evidence
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to an unsupported prose assertion in the conclusion; deleting or hedging it leaves every theorem, algorithm, and numerical guarantee intact, so the repair is short and local with no mathematical loss.
